\textbf{Solution:} From the construction, we have that $MN$ bisects $BC$ perpendicularly,\\
$\therefore DB=DC$,\\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of $\triangle ACD = AC+AD+CD = AC+AD+BD = AC+AB = 5+12 = \boxed{17}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure there is triangle ABC, the base BA is a horizontal line, point D is located on line segment BA; the dashed circular arcs drawn from points B and C intersect at M and N, connecting M and N gives an oblique straight line, and this straight line passes through D; the figure also connects C and D, forming triangle ACD. Then reason: according to the construction property of drawing arcs with B and C as centers and the same radius and intersecting at M and N, line MN is the perpendicular bisector of line segment BC. Because D is on MN, the distances from D to B and C are equal, that is, DB = DC. The perimeter of triangle ACD is AC + AD + CD. Substituting CD = DB, the perimeter = AC + AD + DB. Also because in the figure D is on line segment AB, AD + DB = AB. Therefore the perimeter = AC + AB = 5 + 12 = 17.
